cards.title: The optimal complexity of Klee's measure problem in higher dimensions
cards.formal: For every fixed integer d≥3, determine the optimal deterministic worst-case running time, up to constant factors as n→∞, for computing the exact d-dimensional volume of the union of n axis-aligned boxes in the arithmetic real-RAM model below. The dimension may affect constants and the algorithm, but is not an input parameter in this running-time question.
cards.why: A basic measure-computation problem underlying geometric union and coverage algorithms.

progress.text: An exact O(n^(d/2)) static algorithm is obtained for fixed d≥3; separate word-RAM improvements use integer-coordinate assumptions.
Faster box-union approximation and a general object-query lower bound are published.
Exact dynamic data structures achieve near-optimal amortized update bounds under a stated combinatorial clique hypothesis, leaving the present unconditional static classification separate.

cards.definitions: An input is a list of n≥0 closed boxes B_i=∏_{j=1}^d [a_i,j,b_i,j], specified by their 2dn finite real endpoints, with a_i,j≤b_i,j. Overlaps, coincident endpoints, duplicate boxes and zero side lengths are allowed. The output is the exact Lebesgue measure of ∪_i B_i, returned as a real number; the empty union has volume zero. For clarity, the real-RAM convention here is deterministic computation with exact real registers, unit-cost copying, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by nonzero values, comparisons and branching. Random access is through integer addresses. Control and address registers have O(log(n+2)) bits, with any fixed constant factor depending on the algorithm and d; standard arithmetic, comparison, Boolean and shift operations on these words cost one unit. Integers can be converted to real registers, but real values can affect integer control only through comparisons: no floor, bit extraction or arbitrary real-to-integer conversion is available. A program is finite and independent of n and the coordinates; any hard-coded real constants must be algebraic and finitely specified. Input reads, output writes, preprocessing, memory operations and control steps count. Worst-case time is the maximum over all endpoint lists of size n, regardless of coordinate magnitude. The requested precision is a Θ bound: logarithmic factors count, and constants may depend on d. No randomness, approximation tolerance, oracle or precomputed advice depending on n is supplied.
cards.answer_criterion: For each fixed d≥3, give a rate T_d(n), an exact algorithm with worst-case time O(T_d(n)), and an unconditional lower bound Ω(T_d(n)) for every correct algorithm in the same model. If no single rate is attainable within constant factors, establishing that failure of asymptotic optimality also answers the stated optimal-time request. An improved upper bound alone, a conditional lower bound, a restriction to particular box shapes, or a result only for approximate or dynamic volume does not complete the classification.

context_blocks.title: Overlap counts only once
context_blocks.text: Two boxes may cover the same region, so adding their individual volumes overcounts their intersection. In three dimensions, [0,2]³ and [1,3]×[0,2]² each have volume 8, but their union has volume 12. The task requests this single total volume; it does not request a full description of the union boundary. In higher dimensions a box is simply a product of intervals.

context_blocks.title: The known exact bound
context_blocks.text: Chan’s 2013 algorithm computes the union volume in O(n^(d/2)) time for every fixed d≥3. This gives n^(3/2) in dimension three and n² in dimension four. The unresolved target is a matching classification of the fastest possible exact computation. The known relationship with clique problems supplies conditional evidence for the exponent, rather than a matching unconditional lower bound for all algorithms.

context_blocks.title: Why numerical conventions matter
context_blocks.text: The real-RAM question counts an arithmetic operation on a coordinate as one step even when the coordinate would require many bits to encode. Chan also obtains logarithmic improvements for integer coordinates in a word-RAM setting. Those improvements do not automatically transfer to unrestricted real inputs, and the source explicitly discusses this distinction. The detailed primitive and worst-case conventions above make the inherited real-RAM target explicit.

context_blocks.title: Recent advances concern other guarantees
context_blocks.text: The SoCG 2025 work speeds up approximation of union volume and proves a lower bound for algorithms restricted to certain object queries. A small relative error is permitted there. The ICALP 2026 work maintains exact volume under insertions and deletions and measures amortized update time. Both are significant results, but neither determines the unconditional optimal time of a single exact static computation in this card’s model.

sentences: Klee’s measure problem asks for the volume covered by a union of axis-aligned boxes.
Overlapping regions count once, and only the exact total volume is required.
For each fixed dimension at least three, the question seeks matching worst-case time bounds in a specified arithmetic real-RAM model.
Chan’s general upper bound is O(n^(d/2)), with no matching unconditional classification supplied by the checked later work.
Recent approximation and dynamic advances answer different questions.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.

benchmark_selection.basis: Individual editorial review of saved titles, importance rationales, problem statements, source notes and working summaries. This is a review of importance and topical diversity, not a fresh verification of open status or completion of draft formulations. Importance scores are preserved.
